Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call today. As discussed, Stonebridge Labs is ready to move from a feature exploration to a focused technical validation for the Navigator integration with Redwood. The goal for this phase is to:

- Validate end-to-end calls from our orchestration to Redwood hosted endpoints (auth + routing).
- Run scenario-driven QA around latency and cache behavior for our average query length (~220 tokens).
- Verify fallback behavior for model variant mismatch and rate limiting.
- Establish a runbook for our SREs to use during canary and production rollouts.

We can provide a staging tenant and a set of synthetic workloads. What we need from Redwood: a proposed test matrix, a short list of environment/access requirements (keys, allowed IPs), and an initial runbook draft we can co-edit.

Attached is our integration requirements doc (stonebridge-integration-requirements.pdf) and a spreadsheet with preferred test scenarios.

Proposed week for the work: Sept 7–10. Doable on your side?

Appreciate it — happy to sync live early next week if helpful.

Best,
Lucia

Lucia / Kimberly — quick note from the engineering validation perspective. Below is the test matrix I suggest; I attached an editable spreadsheet version.

Test matrix (overview):
- Happy-path functional: 50 scripted prompts, model variant A (gpt-3.4x), sequence length median 220 tokens -> verify correct structured output and 200 OK.
- Latency profile: 95p under 350ms for single-shot prompts; measure cold vs warm KB cache.
- Load bursts: 250 rps sustained for 2 minutes (verify autoscale triggers and no token truncation).
- Cache behavior: prefix/KV cache warm-up test; ensure no stale KV reads when we roll model versions.
- Fallbacks: simulate model A unavailable -> route to model B (quantized) and evaluate time-to-first-token delta and regressed outputs.
- Security checklist: TLS mutual auth (if you prefer), request/response logging controls, and retention TTL confirmation.

Artifacts we need from Stonebridge: staging cluster endpoint, test user accounts, one example of payloads that have >1k tokens (for truncation checks), and any enterprise audit requirements.

Credentials: please place sandbox creds in the secure doc you shared or send via your vault. We will only use them for the scheduled window; keys will be rotated afterwards.

Attachments: sb-test-cases.xlsx (detailed scenarios)

I recommend we run a dry-run of two happy-path scenarios during the pre-check to validate telemetry ingestion (traces + token-level cost). Can someone from your SREs confirm observability endpoint access?

—Sergio
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
